items.title: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
items.description: Broadcom has released security updates to fix a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass vulnerability that Chinese-linked hackers have exploited in zero-day attacks since September 2026. [...]

items.title: Qwen Incidents Show Self-Hosted AI Models Need Stronger Steering
items.description: Companies deploying AI agents have the illusion of control, but several incidents demonstrate that businesses need to be ready to enforce directions.

items.title: Hackers steal data of 1.6 million SBC Medical Group customers
items.description: SBC Medical Group has warned in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) that two cybersecurity incidents exposed sensitive customer and employee information, including personal data belonging to 1.6 million people. [...]

items.title: ASUS warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express
items.description: ASUS released Control Center Express v1.7.29 to fix three critical vulnerabilities that could let remote attackers gain administrative control of the management console and the devices it manages. [...]

items.title: Second Norwegian Energy Company Breached in Two Days
items.description: No specific link has been drawn between the two incidents, though they certainly sing the same notes.

items.title: Critical PHP Flaws Allow Code Execution, But Don't Panic 'PHP2Shell'-Style
items.description: November's monthly security release patches seven critical PHP flaws that should be addressed ASAP, though experts say exploitability varies and depends heavily on configuration.

items.title: Navigating Vulnerability Hysteria in the AI Era
items.description: This installment of the Reporters' Notebook video series examines the fallout from recent high-severity flaw disclosures, exploring how fears of AI-assisted exploits trigger widespread panic, operational disruptions, and growing warning fatigue.

items.title: Newly Patched VMware vCenter Flaw Exploited as Zero-Day by Chinese APT
items.description: Google says a China-linked espionage group exploited a critical VMware vCenter authentication bypass before Broadcom released a patch. The post Newly Patched VMware vCenter Flaw Exploited as Zero-Day by Chinese APT appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: ThreatsDay: GPT-6.2 Jailbreak Flaws, BubbleLoader PNG Malware, $500M Ransom Demands + 17 More Stories
items.description: The easiest way to fool someone is to give them something they already expect. A job offer. A message about a service outage. A familiar app. Nothing looks strange at first. And that's the problem. This week's stories show how ordinary things are being used to steal data, spread malware, and get people to hand over access. There's another shift worth watching. AI is making some attacks easier
